perspective:
Keith’s available information:

- Keith and Elizabeth are colleagues at a construction company: Keith is a construction worker, Elizabeth is the receptionist. They have a friendly but professional relationship, mainly interacting when Keith visits the office for paperwork/project updates.
- Keith noticed Elizabeth had been unusually curt with him over several days. He wondered if he had upset her, possibly through a misunderstanding or an unknown mistake.
- Keith asked Elizabeth if he had done something to upset her. Elizabeth denied it, said she was dealing with personal stuff, and apologized if she seemed short.
- Keith felt sympathetic and offered to listen, suggesting a coffee break. Elizabeth thanked him and accepted.
- Over coffee, Elizabeth shared more about her stresses. Keith perceived them as quite severe. He thought professional help might benefit her but was concerned about offending her.
- Keith told Elizabeth he appreciated her sharing and asked if she had considered talking to a professional. Elizabeth said she had thought about it but was unsure and hesitant about seeking help.
- Afterward, Keith noticed Elizabeth became slightly withdrawn. He believed his suggestion might have embarrassed her and felt regretful.
- Keith told her he hoped he had not overstepped and said he was there to support her. Elizabeth said he had not overstepped, appreciated his concern, and said it was a lot to think about.
- Later, Elizabeth seemed more open and appreciative of Keith’s concern. Keith believed she valued his support and felt more comfortable around him.
- Keith told Elizabeth he was glad they talked and that he is always available if she needs to chat or take a break. Elizabeth thanked him, said it meant a lot, and that she felt better knowing she had his support.
- Keith intends to maintain this supportive relationship with Elizabeth.
